This view reveals an important cognitive asymmetry in the AI coding era: when architects fully delegate code implementation to AI, they actually lose first-hand sensory access to evaluating solution feasibility. The traditional view holds that architects should "focus on architecture design and leave implementation to the team"—this model assumes architects maintain system understanding through code reviews and team feedback. But Dennis points out that in the AI-generated code scenario, this feedback loop is broken: AI-generated code varies in quality, and the generation process is invisible to the architect (black box), turning architecture reviews into a formal "looks reasonable" exercise rather than a substantive "understand its impact on the system."
